comment: Where the NVIDIA runtime for DLSS comes from. Read by the editor plugin (nvidia_runtime.gd) and tools/fetch_nvidia_sdk.py. Nothing listed here is part of this addon: the files are fetched from NVIDIA's release on the developer's machine, after the developer accepted NVIDIA's licences.
fg_files_comment: The DLSS Frame Generation DLLs (Phase 3). They ship with exports (they are in export_files) but are only loaded at runtime when Frame Generation is enabled and the GPU supports it (a GeForce RTX 40 series or newer); otherwise they sit unused. nvngx_dlssg.dll is under the NVIDIA RTX SDKs licence (like nvngx_dlss.dll); the sl.* DLLs are MIT (Streamline).
licences_comment: The licences to accept are the licence files of the pinned release: 'file' is the file in the archive (its SHA-256 is in nvidia_runtime.lock.json), 'text' the same file at the release's commit on GitHub. The editor dialog and tools/fetch_nvidia_sdk.py --show-licences show 'text' only after checking that its SHA-256 is the locked one, so the text accepted is the text that ships with the DLLs. 'acceptance' says whether the developer has to accept a licence (the NVIDIA RTX SDKs licence) or only receives it (Streamline's MIT licence); the acceptance record lists both, marking which were accepted.

licences.name: NVIDIA RTX SDKs licence (the DLSS runtime: nvngx_dlss.dll and nvngx_dlssg.dll)
Streamline licence (MIT, sl.*.dll)
licences.acceptance: not required: the MIT licence, for sl.*.dll. The NSight Perf SDK licence it also names covers only sl_nvperf.*, which this runtime does not include.
